chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ahmad ibn Hamzah, who said:

I said to him, 'In our land, sometimes a will is made bequeathing wealth to the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and they bring it to me. I dislike carrying it to you until I consult you.' He said, 'Do not bring it to me, and do not present it to me.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about bringing the wealth of the Family of Muhammad to him when it is bequeathed in wills?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ahmad ibn Hamzah seeks guidance from Imam al-Rida (or the relevant Imam depending on the specific chain's attribution in the full context, often cited as Imam al-Rida or Imam al-Jawad in similar contexts regarding Ahl al-Bayt's wealth) concerning the practice of delivering bequeathed property to the Family of Muhammad. The Imam’s concise response, 'Do not bring it to me, nor present it to me,' reflects a nuanced juristic preference (istihbab) or specific legal ruling regarding the direct handling of their share of inheritance or bequests, distinguishing it from general distribution practices. This highlights the scholarly attention to the precise administration of wealth designated for the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring it aligns with their discretion and legal status.
